Memory loss, difficulty understanding conversation and other cognitive difficulties are commonly associated with migraine attacks.

Difficulty thinking during a migraine attack is often attributed to the pain.

I definitely have to disagree with pain being considered the cause of migraine brain fog.

I have 24/7 migraine and pain and brain fog don't go hand in hand. I experience them at different times. When I get spikes in pain it's incredibly rare for me to also have brain-fog (and a bunch of other non-pain symptoms I get) at the same time.This makes much more sense:

researchers argue that cognitive dysfunction appears to less about the pain and more about the brain’s activity during the migraine. One reason for this is that cognitive dysfunction arises in the earliest stage of a migraine attack, even before the pain begins. Even when acute medications work for the pain, cognitive dysfunction can remain.

I never realised that what I get were cognitive difficulties, they happen only occasionally (~1x a month) and it sucks when it happens - it explains why I act like 5yo... find it hard to follow conversations, dropping things, difficult to read a menu and making poor, poor decisions like walking into 3 lanes of oncoming traffic. I find the cognitive dysfunction a lot more incapacitating then the pain, which is saying something.
I hate when I get the Stupids. It's so frustrating, although with me, the pain is still worse.
